IS MADE AS UNDER:
 ORAL ORDER Sri.H.M.Patel., counsel for the petitioner and Smt.Archana P.Tiwari., AAG along with Sri.Sheshadri Jaishankar.M., AGA for respondents 1 and 2 have appeared in person.
A perusal of the office note depicts that notice to respondent No.3 is held sufficient vide order dated 12.08.2024.
He has neither engaged the services of an advocate or conducted the case as a party in person.

2. The short facts are these :
It is said that the petitioner is the owner of land bearing Sy.No.6 measuring to an extent of 08 Acres 05 Guntas situated at Wagadari Village, Aland Taluk, Kalaburagi District.
The Government of Karnataka acquired the land for percolation tank.
A Notification under Section 4(1) and 6(1) were issued.
The Special land Acquisition Officer passed the award on NC: 2025:KHC-K:5119 HC-KAR 04.05.2009 in the name of the petitioner awarding compensation of Rs.38,500/- per acre.
One Mr.Shivasamba S/o.Mahadevayya filed objections in the office of the SLAO for the disbursement of the compensation amount.
The SLAO, Kalaburagi referred the matter to the Civil Court Senior Division, Aland under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act for the apportionment of compensation.
The third respondent filed a petition under Section 30 of the Act, claiming compensation amount and the same was registered as Misc. No.13/2009 instead of registering as LAC.
The reference Court after recording the evidence of both the parties, passed the order on 21.07.2015 and rejected the claim of the third respondent.

sentences.text: As the matter stood thus, the petitioner moved an application to the reference Court on 11.08.2015 for release of deposited amount awarded by the SLAO under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act and deposited under Section 30 of the Act.
The Reference Court rejected the application of the petitioner on 01.10.2015.
Under these circumstances, the petitioner is before this Court.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5119 HC-KAR 3.
Counsel for the respective parties urged several contentions.
Heard the arguments and perused the Writ papers with care.
4. The facts are sufficiently said and do not require reiteration.
The issue falls within a narrow compass and relates to the rejection of the claim for release of the deposited amount in favor of the petitioner.
It is not in dispute that the land in question was acquired and an award was passed in the name of the petitioner in 2009.
The Reference Court after the receipt of reference under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, adjudicated the dispute and rejected the claim of the third respondent.

The request of the petitioner to release the deposited amount has been rejected on the sole ground that there is no specific order of the SLAO, Kalaburagi to release the deposited amount in favor of the petitioner.
The rejection is untenable.
The reason is simple.
It is not in dispute that pursuant to the objection filed by the third respondent, the SLAO deposited the award amount before the Reference Court.
It is significant to note that the claim of the third respondent was rejected.
Once the claim is rejected, the Reference Court NC: 2025:KHC-K:5119 HC-KAR had no option except to release the award amount in favor of the awardee i.e., the petitioner.
There is no need for a specific order of the SLAO to release the deposited amount.
For the reasons stated above, the order passed by the Reference Court is liable to be set-aside.
Accordingly, it is set -aside.
5. The Writ of Certiorari is ordered.
The order dated 01.10.2015 passed by the Reference Court vide Annexure-D is quashed.
The amount deposited by the SLAO shall be released in favor of the petitioner after due identification within four weeks from the receipt of certified copy of this order.
6. Resultantly, the Writ Petition is allowed.
